# Exact all-normal depth of the fourth dilate of the reflexive-triangle product

This is a finite exact algebraic certificate for one actual mixed-integer
product. It is not a proof of OC. Together with the separately proved
martingale inequality, it supplies an actual globally critical profile whose
entire nonnegative convex-potential cone has efficiency below Gamma_2,
even though every proper closed-minor count quota is strict.

## 1. The actual set and theorem

Put

    D4=conv{(-4,-4),(4,0),(0,4)},
    P=D4 intersect Z^2
     ={(x,y) in Z^2:min(-x-y,2x-y,2y-x)>=-4}.

Let K be any nondegenerate triangle, V its area, g its centroid, and
lambda_0,lambda_1,lambda_2 its barycentric coordinate functions. On
S=P times K use the measure which sums ordinary area over the fibers.
There are 31 fibers, so the total mass is 31V.

**Theorem.** Every closed ambient halfspace containing (0,g) has mass at
least 40V/3. The maximum raw halfspace depth on S is exactly 40V/3.
Consequently its normalized maximum depth is 40/93.

The proof below consists of an elementary reduction and a finite certificate
of homogeneous cubic nonnegativity. Every certificate operation is an
integer or rational arithmetic operation. No numerical optimization,
unverified sign, or limiting extrapolation is used.

## 2. Upper bound and a point in the actual set

Define ell_0(z)=-z1-z2, ell_1(z)=2z1-z2, ell_2(z)=2z2-z1 and

    H_j={lambda_j(x)-1/3+ell_j(z)>=0}.

For each j, the offsets on P have twelve positive entries, three zero
entries, and sixteen negative entries. The positive-offset fibers are
strictly fully captured, the negative ones strictly missed, and the
zero-offset fibers each contribute 4V/9. Thus every H_j has mass
12V+3(4V/9)=40V/3. Their defining margins sum identically to zero.
Therefore these three closed halfspaces cover the full ambient space and
give the upper bound 40V/3 on the depth of every point. The proposed
lower-bound point belongs to S because 0 belongs to P and g belongs to K.

The elementary counts can also be obtained by enumerating the 81 integer
pairs in [-4,4]^2 and retaining the displayed three inequalities. This
finite enumeration is performed independently in the verifier.

## 3. Compact parameterization of all through-source halfspaces

A containing halfspace can be translated parallel to its boundary until
that boundary passes through (0,g), only decreasing its captured mass.
Write the resulting margin as L(z)+u dot (x-g), with L a linear functional
of the integer coordinates. The three base vertex values at
(1,0),(0,1),(-1,-1) sum to zero, as do the continuous vertex values of
u dot (x-g). Independent permutations of the base and continuous triangle
vertices preserve P and its counting measure, preserve uniform area on K,
and preserve the family of ambient halfspaces. The base permutations are
integer linear bijections: they permute the integer vertices of the
integer three-vertex configuration and their inverses do likewise; their two-by-two determinants are +1 or -1.
The continuous permutations are affine area-preserving bijections of K.
These operations do not replace the lattice by a different lattice.

After these permutations, sort both triples decreasingly. Unless the
normal is zero, the sum of their largest entries is positive. Divide all
entries by this sum. Then all possibilities are represented by

    L(z)=a z1+b z2,
    (h0,h1,h2)=(1-a,c,-1+a-c),
    0<=a<=1, -a/2<=b<=a,
    -(1-a)/2<=c<=1-a.                              (1)

This compact parameter domain is the tetrahedron with vertices

    (0,0,-1/2), (0,0,1), (1,-1/2,0), (1,1,0).

Use its barycentric coordinates tau_i>=0, sum tau_i=1. Thus

    a=tau2+tau3,
    b=-tau2/2+tau3,
    c=-tau0/2+tau1.                                (2)

For z=(x,y), twice the three fiber vertex margins are the linear forms

    f0=(2,2,2x-y,2x+2y) dot tau,
    f1=(-1,2,2x-y,2x+2y) dot tau,
    f2=(-1,-4,2x-y,2x+2y) dot tau.                 (3)

Their differences, independent of z, are

    g0=f1-f2=(0,6,0,0) dot tau,
    g1=f0-f2=(3,6,0,0) dot tau,
    g2=f0-f1=(3,0,0,0) dot tau.                   (4)

All three g's are nonnegative throughout the parameter tetrahedron.

## 4. The exact cubic inequality

For three distinct ordered values r0>r1>r2 of an affine function at the
vertices of a uniform triangle, the relative area where that function is
nonnegative is

    [(r1-r2)(r0)_+^2-(r0-r2)(r1)_+^2
                         +(r0-r1)(r2)_+^2]
       /[(r0-r1)(r0-r2)(r1-r2)].                  (5)

For completeness, if the threshold zero is between the highest and middle
values, the captured region is a similar corner triangle, of area fraction
r0^2/[(r0-r1)(r0-r2)]. This is (5), as only r0 is positive.
If zero is between the middle and lowest values, apply the same corner
formula to the missed triangle and subtract it from one; expansion gives
(5). If all three are nonpositive the numerator is zero. If all three are
nonnegative, expansion of the numerator gives the denominator. Supporting
thresholds follow directly or by continuity. These cases prove (5).

Apply (5) with the margins (3). For g0g1g2>0, the sum of captured fiber
fractions equals N/(g0g1g2), where

    N=sum_(z in P)[g0(f0(z))_+^2-g1(f1(z))_+^2
                                      +g2(f2(z))_+^2].

It is therefore enough to prove on the entire parameter tetrahedron

    S=3N-40g0g1g2 >=0.                             (6)

Notice that all f and g forms were doubled together; each term has degree
three, so the common factor cancels. The coefficient 40 in (6) proves the
raw fraction 40/3 exactly.

## 5. A polynomial lower bound on each rational tetrahedron

Let T have four rational vertices. On T each linear form has its extrema
at vertices. Replace each positive term g0(f0)_+^2 or g2(f2)_+^2 by its
full square if its f is nonnegative at every vertex; otherwise replace that
term by zero. Replace -g1(f1)_+^2 by zero if f1 is nonpositive everywhere;
otherwise replace it by -g1 f1^2. As the g's are nonnegative, each
replacement is a pointwise lower bound. Retain -40g0g1g2 unchanged.
Call the resulting homogeneous cubic S_T. Then S>=S_T on T.

Write a point of T in local barycentric coordinates xi_0,...,xi_3.
If every coefficient of the degree-three expansion of S_T in those
coordinates is nonnegative, then S_T>=0 on T. Equivalently every cubic
Bernstein coefficient is nonnegative; the power coefficient differs by
only a positive multinomial factor. This implication includes all faces,
edges, and vertices, with no strict-sign assumption.

For exact storage, a vertex is a nonzero nonnegative integer vector v,
representing v/sum(v) in the original tau coordinates. Expanding first
with v instead of v/sum(v) preserves every coefficient's sign: the
coefficient of xi_i xi_j xi_k is multiplied by the single positive factor
sum(v_i)sum(v_j)sum(v_k). The certificate can therefore use integer
coefficients throughout the sign checks.

## 6. The finite exact decomposition and its verification

The proof data are the complete file

    ../assets/pk-nov6/computations/r4_exact_bernstein_tetra_attempt_slab_recovery.json

(SHA-256 2290a0a5b25f1264cc4c48e9c4e596af59ec93bd5cdc8392ece91aaad6566d52).
It lists 69 integer split planes and a rooted tree of 15,099 records.
A record is either `proved` or specifies one of those planes. The children
of a split are determined by the following explicit formulas, so no
unlisted triangulation or numerical coordinates enter the proof.

If a plane f separates positive vertex p from nonpositive vertices a,b,c,
let A,B,C be its intersections with pa,pb,pc. The children are

    (p,A,B,C), (a,b,c,A), (b,c,A,B), (c,A,B,C).       (7)

If positive vertices are p,q and nonpositive vertices a,b, let
A=pa, B=pb, C=qa, D=qb be the corresponding intersections. The children are

    (p,A,B,q), (A,B,q,C), (B,q,C,D),
    (a,A,C,b), (A,C,b,B), (C,b,B,D).                (8)

For three positive vertices reverse the plane. In homogeneous integer
coordinates the crossing intersection of positive v and nonpositive w is

    primitive(f(v)w-f(w)v),                        (9)

where primitive divides by the gcd of the coordinates. Zero-determinant
children are discarded. The nonzero children in (7) and (8) are the usual
corner-tetrahedron/triangular-prism decompositions; the verifier also
checks the following stronger exact conditions separately at every node.

1. Every child vertex is in all four parent facet halfspaces.
2. The exact child volumes sum to the exact parent volume.
3. Every pair of children has a separating facet plane, so their interiors
   are disjoint.

For an integer-ray tetrahedron (v0,...,v3), its volume relative to the
original parameter simplex is

    abs(det(v0,...,v3))/product_i sum(v_i).

Facet halfspaces are computed by exact signed 3-by-3 minors. Conditions
1--3 imply that the children cover the whole parent, not just almost all
of it. Indeed their finite union is closed. Any missing parent point
would have a relatively open neighborhood disjoint from the union; that
neighborhood contains parent interior points and hence positive volume,
contradicting condition 2 and interior disjointness. This also accounts
for parent boundary points and all zero-sign degeneracies.

The standalone implementation

    ../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_r4_all_normal_bernstein_certificate_slab_recovery.py

(SHA-256 f102c2c29e9b74c16b4af34440a8338dd0eeeec5ce3261203cfaf9e7734f52c2)
is a direct finite verifier of these statements. It imports only standard
Python integer/Fraction operations and does not import the search code.
It independently expands S_T in the ordinary power basis. It checks that
all records are reached once, every internal record has exactly all its
specified children, and every terminal record has all twenty cubic power
coefficients nonnegative. Its exact result is

    PASS: 525779 exact checks;
    11188 complete nonnegative power/Bernstein leaves;
    3911 verified disjoint covering splits; maximum depth 15.

Thus induction from the leaves to the root proves (6) on the full
parameter tetrahedron. The JSON is an explicit finite algebraic proof
certificate, and the verifier specifies all its arithmetic. The search
program only found this certificate; no output of its heuristic choices
is needed without verification. There are no unproved or pending leaves.

## 7. Repeated heights and closed pure-base caps

The cubic certificate already proves the bound for distinct continuous
heights. When the continuous normal is nonzero but heights repeat,
approximate the normal by normals with distinct heights. On every fiber
the limiting cut hyperplane has ordinary area zero. Its indicator
therefore converges almost everywhere, and bounded convergence over the
finite sum of fibers transfers the same lower bound. This includes every
supporting or through-vertex cut.

For a pure-base normal, approximate it by through-source normals having
nonzero continuous parts. At every point of S, the limsup of their closed
cap indicators is at most the indicator of the limiting CLOSED pure-base
cap: strictly negative base margins eventually remain negative; zero base
margins are already fully included in the closed limit. Since the total
measure is finite, reverse Fatou gives

    mass(closed limiting cap)
       >=limsup mass(approximating caps)>=40V/3.

No mass on whole boundary fibers is discarded. Positive scaling and the
finite permutations used earlier do not affect this argument. We have
now covered every nonzero ambient normal and hence every containing
closed halfspace. Combining this with Section 2 proves the theorem.

## 8. Consequence for the auxiliary potential approach

The source `candidate b78a2eb10bd3783f`
proves independently that every proper nonempty lattice-closed subset
T of P satisfies |T|/31<k(T)/4, and that for the displayed canonical
profile W=(1/3)sum_j 1_Hj the exact optimum over all nonnegative
normal-dependent physically convex potentials is 40/93. That proof uses
an explicit rational martingale with 144 positive entries and has its
own independent verifier. The theorem here removes its previously open
criticality premise: these are now actual globally depth-attaining caps
at the actual mixed point (0,g).

Consequently strict proper-closed-minor count quotas, actual lattice
completeness, equal full fibers, common cap masses, and regular full
section-centroid conditions do NOT imply individual Gamma_2=4/9
potential efficiency. The gap is exactly 4/279. This does not refute a
statement with the further bad-depth/minimum premises, and is not an OC
counterexample: 40/93 is much greater than the OC target 1/9.

## 9. The deepest point is unique

Suppose Y is another point of S of raw depth 40V/3. It cannot lie strictly
inside any canonical H_j. Indeed increasing that cap's threshold slightly
would still retain Y while removing positive area from each of the three
proper zero-offset fibers; all other contributions cannot increase. The
new cap would have raw mass strictly below 40V/3. Thus all three canonical
margins at Y are nonpositive. Their sum is zero, so all three are zero.
Writing Y=(z,x), this gives lambda_j(x)=1/3-ell_j(z). Since ell_j(z) is an
integer and 0<=lambda_j(x)<=1, all ell_j(z) must be zero. Hence z=0 and
x=g. Thus the set of actual deepest integer bases is exactly {0}; it
occupies only one of the four occupied parity classes. The example does
not test a premise requiring deepest bases in every occupied parity class.
